title: step: open PR for lazy Vault tree folder loading
description: Follow the pstack Opening a PR playbook after implementation and verification. Keep commits ordered by verifiable unit.
acceptance_criteria: PR description names the user impact, data shape, verification evidence, limits preserved, and any follow-up work. No commit or push happens unless explicitly authorized by active instructions.
notes:
PR-ready description for lazy Vault tree folder loading

Title: Lazy-load Vault tree folders through the entries endpoint

User impact:
- Large vaults remain navigable even when the bounded initial /api/vault/tree scan hits the 500-node budget.
- The first snapshot stays fast and honest: top-level project folders still appear, and folders fetch children only when opened.
- The prior warning now explains that this is a partial initial snapshot, not a host outage.

Data shape and architecture:
- Backend runtime listVaultEntries accepts an optional cursor and preserves the existing 200-entry page limit.
- BFF GET /api/vault/entries parses path + cursor, keeps ACL checks ahead of Brain RPC, and forwards cursor to vault.list.
- Web API adds typed VaultEntry/VaultEntriesResponse plus fetchVaultEntries(path, cursor?).
- VaultView now uses normalized tree state: nodesByPath, rootIds, directoriesByPath, expandedPaths, selectedPath, focusKey, treeMeta.
- Directory state models unloaded, loading, loaded, refreshing, loadingMore, and error, including nextCursor/truncated metadata.
- Tree UI renders Load folder, Loading, Retry, and Load more rows as needed; expansion triggers /api/vault/entries.
- Deep links open files while loading known missing ancestors, and known file rows do not trigger directory-entry fetches.

Limits preserved:
- The bounded recursive tree scan remains in place; VAULT_TREE_MAX_NODES is not raised.
- VAULT_TREE_MAX_DEPTH and VAULT_LIST_PAGE_LIMIT behavior remain intact.
- The browser still receives metadata for visible tree nodes plus opened-file content, not all vault file bodies.

Verification evidence:

title: checkpoint: shared mutable state for Vault lazy-load
description: Feature playbook throughput checkpoint using separate-before-serializing-shared-state. Identify shared mutable targets such as VaultView tree state, polling refresh, expanded paths, selected path, and per-directory load requests.
acceptance_criteria: Checkpoint notes define the single owner or separated state structure for tree data, loaded-directory status, cursors, in-flight requests, polling reconciliation, and stale response handling.
notes:
Shared mutable state checkpoint:

Decision: tree browsing state has one reducer owner. VaultView keeps non-tree UI state and effect orchestration only. Do not coordinate competing setState calls by convention.

Reducer-owned state: nodesByPath, rootIds, directoriesByPath, expandedPaths, selectedPath, treeMeta, and treeFocusKey or focusEpoch if TreeList still needs remounting for programmatic focus.

Directory state is a discriminated union: unloaded; loading { requestId, staleData? }; loaded { childIds, nextCursor, truncated, loadedAtMs, pageCount }; refreshing { requestId, childIds, nextCursor, truncated, loadedAtMs, pageCount }; loadingMore { requestId, childIds, nextCursor, truncated, loadedAtMs, pageCount }; error { error, failedAtMs, stale, childIds?, nextCursor?, truncated?, loadedAtMs?, pageCount? }.

VaultView-owned state remains separate: readerContent, readerError, isLoadingFile, openRequestIdRef, search query/results/loading/empty, edit capability state, deep-link props/effect orchestration, poll timers, focus listeners, and request-id counters. Effects may create ids and dispatch actions, but the reducer writes tree state.

Compatibility rule: recursive VaultTreeNode[] from /api/vault/tree is an input snapshot only. Adapter normalizes it. Render adapter derives TreeList items and synthetic rows from normalized state. Synthetic rows are not fake vault nodes.

Race rules: root polls carry requestId and stale responses are ignored. Root polling reconciles roots and node metadata only, preserving loaded directory children for existing directory paths. Transient poll failure marks stale and preserves visible data; auth or ACL-deny failures may clear fail-closed. Directory refresh, load-more, and expansion responses apply only when { path, requestId } matches active state. Collapse does not clear cached children. Newer refresh beats older load-more. Deep-link focus expands ancestors and triggers missing ancestor loads without overwriting newer focus. File open state remains independent from tree loading.
close_reason: Completed Feature playbook throughput checkpoints. Evidence: blocking gates, independent workstreams, shared mutable state ownership/race rules, and smallest safe decomposition recorded in notes.
